title: Central Teke language - Wikipedia
text: Central Teke is a member of the Teke languages dialect continuum of the Congolese plateau. Central Teke dialects are Ngungwel and Mpu, Boo, and Nzikou.

title: Teke-Nzikou Language (NZU) – L1 & L2 Speakers... | Ethnologue Free
text: Teke-Nzikou is a stable indigenous language of Congo. It belongs to the Niger-Congo language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.

title: Teke-Nzikou / Central Teke
text: Teke-Nzikou and Teke-Eboo are dialects of the same language. Some Tekes say there is no word for a thousand in Teke. Pfuuna is mostly used for money, and means 5,000 cfa.
